rules.treatment: No price adjustment on ex-date; the PR index is not adjusted (PAF = none). TR/NTR indexes reinvest the cash dividend on ex-date.

Classified special and PR-adjusted via PAF = (CumPx − Div) / CumPx only when the dividend is ≥5% of market price; below 5% it is treated as ordinary with no PR adjustment. TR/NTR indexes reinvest regardless of classification.
Treated identically to a stock split: PAF padj = pt-1 × A / (A+B); no divisor change; PR index adjusted.
No price adjustment; shares multiplied by the bonus ratio; market cap unchanged; no divisor adjustment.
PAF padj = pt-1 × A / (A+B); divisor unchanged; market cap unchanged.
Child added as a detached security at the when-issued price when available, else zero, held until a real price is available; parent's value deducted on ex-date.

Adjusts only in-the-money rights (subscription price below market) using the when-issued / theoretical price (TERP); out-of-the-money rights are ignored (PAF = 1). Shares increased as of close of ex-date; NOS/FIF/DIF changes threshold 5%/10%/25% by Standard/Small/Micro cap tier.

Applied (PAF + divisor) when the share-count change meets the size threshold — ≥5% of pre-event NOS for Standard, ≥10% Small Cap, ≥25% Micro Cap — with 2 full business days advance notice; changes <±1% on post-event NOS deferred to the next Index Review.

New shares counted toward NOS; adjustment applied when the change meets the size threshold (≥5%/10%/25% by cap tier), with a simultaneous primary + private placement sized jointly; changes <±1% on post-event NOS deferred to the next Index Review.

Treated as a special dividend: extraordinary (vs dividend policy/history) → PAF applied using the gross amount and reinvested in DTR indexes; regular → treated as a normal cash dividend, reinvested in DTR indexes regardless of size.
Target deleted when the deal is unconditional (no fixed % threshold), at last traded price; acquirer share-count change triggers adjustment at 5%/10%/25% by Standard/Small/Micro cap tier.

Deletion when the tender offer is formally completed (no % acceptance threshold and no advance notice — MSCI waits for completion rather than deleting at an acceptance level); removed at tender price or last traded price.

Deleted as soon as possible on a bankruptcy / protection-from-creditors filing when a return to normal business is unlikely; removed at the last traded price, else an OTC / equivalent market price, else the lowest system price (0.00001), with 2 full business days notice.

No price adjustment on ex-date; an ordinary dividend affects only Total Return (TR) and Net Total Return (NTR) indices, not the Price Return index (PAF = none). TR/NTR indices reinvest the dividend on ex-date.

Treated as a corporate action with price and divisor adjustment: the stock's price is adjusted (reduced) by the payment amount at the opening of the effective date. Classification is qualitative — outside the normal historical payment pattern (e.g. described as "special", "extra", "irregular", or "return of capital"); the third consecutive same-timing non-ordinary dividend is reclassified as ordinary (timing, not amount).
Treated identically to a stock split: shares increased and price decreased by the same adjustment factor (e.g. a 5% stock dividend is a 1.05-for-1 split). Market capitalization unchanged.

Treated identically to a stock split / stock dividend: shares increased and price decreased by the same factor, with only the quoting convention differing. Bonus shares not entitled to a later dividend are applied on ex-date, with the later dividend adjusted down over the enlarged share count.
Shares increased (multiplied) and price decreased (divided) by the same adjustment factor; market capitalization unchanged; no divisor change.

Spin-off security added to the parent's indices at a zero price at the close of the day before the ex-date, with no divisor adjustment; the parent is not price-adjusted downward. If the spin-off does not trade for 20 consecutive trading days after the ex-date, it may be removed at zero.

Only in-the-money rights (subscription price below the prior close) are recognized; the price adjustment (TERP) is applied at the opening of the ex-date and shares are increased at the full rights ratio. Out-of-the-money rights are ignored; under/oversubscribed adjustments are made at the next quarterly rebalancing.

Public offerings (including block sales and spot secondaries) receive accelerated implementation only when both thresholds are met: at least 5% of pre-event shares and at least US$150m (a US$1bn+ event is implemented even below 5%). Otherwise implemented at the next quarterly rebalancing.
Non-mandatory; certain private placements are reviewed quarterly and implemented at the quarterly rebalancing, not via accelerated implementation.

Considered a special dividend (price adjusted down at the opening of the effective date), except when declared in lieu of an ordinary cash dividend and fitting the historical pattern in amount and frequency, in which case it is treated as an ordinary cash dividend.

Target deleted on or around the expected delisting or last-trading date, with no minimum threshold for the acquirer's share/IWF change; deletion price is the closing price, or for cash consideration the lower of market close and deal price, for stock consideration a synthetically derived price from the deal ratio. Acquisitions of private/non-index companies are implemented at the next quarterly rebalancing.

Index changes implemented only after final results. A target may be removed early once conditions are met or when remaining free float falls below 15% (even if the offer is still open); the tendered-line replacement is considered once a minimum acceptance ratio of 75% is reached, with one to five business days' notice.
Bankrupt securities are ineligible and removed from all branded indices simultaneously, with a minimum of one day's notice, at the primary-exchange closing price (zero if halted or delisted).

Ordinary (regular) cash dividends are reinvested across the index on the ex date and impact only the total return; there is no price adjustment and no PAF, and the Price Return index is unchanged. Cash (and scrip) dividends with a cash option are treated the same as ordinary cash, except Spanish scrip dividends, which follow the scrip-issue treatment (§4.7). Where a dividend is retracted or corrected, a corrective negative adjustment is applied with T+1 notice; a dividend undetermined on the XD date uses the same-period prior-year amount, or zero if none was paid.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.3 (Unknown and optional ordinary dividends and corrections)

rules.treatment: Classified by description, not by amount: a dividend is special if the distributing company describes it as such, in which case the stock price is adjusted to deduct the dividend amount before the open on the ex date and it is excluded from the total return calculation. A recurring special dividend paid on more than three consecutive non-extraordinary occasions is reclassified as ordinary on the fourth. Where the special dividend is ≥10% of the share price (cum price) with withholding-tax implications, a compensating negative XD adjustment is applied to net-of-tax indices only. No numerical special-vs-ordinary threshold is used for classification.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.4 (Special dividends – tax adjustments)

rules.treatment: Treated as a scrip issue / stock distribution (§4.7): automatic distribution of shares (existing or newly issued) at no charge pro rata to holdings, with a price adjustment factor of shares held before ÷ after; no index divisor adjustment and no change in market capitalisation.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.7 (Scrip issues & stock distributions)

rules.treatment: Treated as a scrip issue (capitalisation / bonus issue) (§4.7): shares distributed at no charge pro rata to existing holdings; the price adjustment factor (shares held before ÷ after) is applied on the ex date; no index divisor adjustment and no change in market capitalisation.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.7 (Scrip issues & stock distributions)

rules.treatment: No index divisor adjustment; the price adjustment factor is shares held before ÷ after (e.g. 0.2 for a 1-into-5 split); applied on the ex date with no change in company market capitalisation.

Parent is price-adjusted by way of a capital repayment; the spun-off entity is added to the same indices as the parent on the ex date at an estimated price using the hierarchy: when-issued price, primary-exchange estimate, company valuation, broker estimate, then the terms of the action. If the spin-off has not traded within 20 business days of the ex date and no firm trading date is announced, it is normally deleted at zero with T+2 notice. Withholding-tax obligations ≥10% of share price trigger a compensating negative XD adjustment to net-of-tax indices only.

Only in-the-money rights (subscription price below market) are recognised: a price adjustment factor (theoretical ex-rights price ÷ cum-rights price) and share increase are applied before the open on the ex date. Out-of-the-money rights get no adjustment. Terms greater than 10-for-1 are ‘highly dilutive’ and use temporary rights and subscription-cash (dummy) lines until the subscription period ends; where the subscription price is unknown on the ex date an estimated value is used, or no adjustment if it cannot be estimated.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.9 (Rights issues/entitlement offers)

rules.treatment: Share and free-float updates from primary and secondary offerings are implemented intra-quarter with at least two days' notice when they meet the materiality threshold — a USD 1bn investable market-cap change, or a 5% index-shares change plus USD 250m — otherwise deferred to the next quarterly review (or the review following discovery if pricing settled more than five business days earlier).
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §5.2 (Intra-quarter updates); §2.1.5 (Timing of corporate actions and events)

rules.treatment: Share and free-float changes from private placements to restricted parties are deferred to the next quarterly review; they do not qualify for the intra-quarter primary/secondary-offering treatment and receive no intra-quarter price or share adjustment.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §5 (Changes to shares outstanding and free float), note 5

rules.treatment: Capital repayments are generally applied with a price adjustment (a capital-repayment PAF of (price − repayment) ÷ price) unless company policy reports regular dividends this way (common in Switzerland), in which case it is treated as an ordinary cash dividend.
rules.source_ref: practitioner: Alex, 2026-09-02 (FTSE 5-day proforma tracker); SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.2 (Ordinary dividends, special dividends and capital repayments); §4.4 (Special dividends – tax adjustments)

rules.treatment: Target is deleted at the last traded price and the acquirer's shares increased per the offer terms once the transaction is deemed final, with a minimum two days' notice; where trading in the target has halted, a synthetic price based on the offer terms is used. For mergers involving elections, FTSE Russell generally waits for the election results before implementing.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.10.2 (Merger between index constituents for stock); §2.1.5 (minimum two-day notice for stock and cash mergers)

rules.treatment: Target normally removed with a minimum T+2 notice when the bidder's holding reaches at least 90% (initial, extension or subsequent) with shares irrevocably accepted for payment, or remaining free float is under 5%, or a compulsory squeeze-out / delisting is confirmed; otherwise a free-float change greater than 3 percentage points is implemented with at least T+2 notice. Deleted at the last traded price, or at a price based on the offer terms if trading has halted.
rules.source_ref: SOURCES/ftse-russell-corporate-actions-guide.pdf §4.11 (Target company deletion); §4.12 (Target company free float change)

rules.treatment: Deleted when FTSE Russell becomes aware of bankruptcy / protection-from-creditors filing, administration, receivership, insolvency or liquidation, with notice — bankruptcy is an ‘actionable’ event carrying a minimum two-day notice. Removed at the last traded price, or an OTC/ineligible-market price if available, else a nominal 0.0001; re-considered after 12 months as a new issue (Russell US and derived indices re-consider at the next reconstitution).
